thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: Elevated tail latency observed on /v1/streaming/generate in us-west-2. Alert triggered: p95 -> 1.8s (SLO 500ms), p99 -> 6.3s. Error rate for streaming chunks up ~2.1%. Auto-escalation to oncall.
oncall-alex: I'm on it. Confirming customers impacted? Any 5xx spike?
sre-maya: 5xx is flat. This looks like tail latency (stalling chunks). I can see large waits on config fetch and auth DB calls in traces. Sample trace: 
```
... waiting for config-fetch (GET /configstore/flags) 1.2s
... auth token lookup (kv-store) 0.9s
... server sending chunk after 800ms stall
```
runtime-dev: I see KC metrics showing KV cache misses spiking at the same time. Sequence: prefix cache miss -> config fetch -> feature flag evaluation -> streaming chunk resumed.
eng-oncall: Is this localized to us-west-2 or global?
sre-maya: Metrics show spike concentrated in us-west-2 control-plane hosts (configstore). us-east-1 and eu-west-1 normal.
support-jordan: Noted two customer tickets reporting long-first-chunk and perceived hangs in streaming UI. Both are us-west customers.
oncall-alex: Quick mitigation suggestions? Can we force cached flags or bypass configstore for streaming paths?
runtime-dev: We have a fallback: if config fetch doesn't reply in 200ms we should default flags from local cache. Looks like the timeout isn't being applied correctly in the streaming path (bug introduced in rollout). I can patch a hotfix to increase timeout and prefer local cache.
sre-maya: Alternative immediate mitigation: route streaming traffic for affected capacity pool to us-east-1 via traffic-policy to avoid control-plane hot hosts. That will cause a small latency increase but avoid stalls. Need deploy-bot to approve route change.
deploy-bot: Routing change PR created: rollback-route/streaming-usw2 -> route-through-use1. Manual approval required.
oncall-alex: Do we want to do route shift while runtime-dev prepares a fix? Which customers need the route vs local fallback?
support-jordan: High-value customers impacted: ACME Analytics (dedicated), BrightRetail (hosted). ACME on Dedicated, prefer no cross-region move — they'd rather we fix control-plane. BrightRetail OK with temporary route.
product-ld: Need to keep SLO conversation short — push for fastest customer-facing fix. If Dedicated customers are impacted we should restore service with fallback rather than cross-region.
runtime-dev: Ok I'll push a hotfix to streaming service that enforces configstore 200ms deadline and uses local last-known flags for in-flight requests. I can build + patch deploy in ~12m.
sre-maya: Meanwhile I'll open a mitigation runbook step: increase configstore read capacity (scale control-plane pod replicas) and identify the root cause of the spike (DB pagination delay). Logs show elevated DB paging latencies on configstore: many queries waiting on the token table pagination.
oncall-alex: Plan: 1) runtime-dev hotfix (local flag fallback) deploy in 12m. 2) sre-maya scale configstore replicas + DB paging mitigation (index/limit tuning) in parallel. 3) If hotfix fails or Dedicated customers still impacted, consider targeted routing for hosted-only customers. 4) Prepare customer comms.
support-jordan: I'll draft comms: "We've identified intermittent streaming stalls tied to control-plane config-fetch latencies in us-west-2. We're deploying a fix to fallback to cached flags and scaling control-plane to restore normal streaming behavior"
next-oncall-ryan: Handoff note: if still degraded at 1743333000 escalate to infra-pg team and open DB slow query investigation.
runtime-dev: Patching now. Build -> canary -> prod deploy. I'll post progress.
sre-maya: Scaling configstore replicas now (replicas +2). DB connections bumped. Monitoring for p95/p99.
incident-bot: Deploy started by runtime-dev (build 17433.5). Canary in 2.
runtime-dev: Canary done, streaming canary p95 down to 480ms, p99 down to 1.1s. Rolling to prod.
incident-bot: Deploy succeeded. Rolling prod.
sre-maya: After scale + hotfix, p95 ~ 350ms, p99 ~ 620ms. Error rate back to baseline. Looks stable for last 5m.
oncall-alex: Great. Summarize customer impact and next steps for handoff.
support-jordan: Impact: ~14 hosted customers saw delayed first-chunk, 2 paid tickets (ACME, BrightRetail). ACME on Dedicated — we did not route them cross-region. No data loss, request retries succeeded.
product-ld: Marking incident as SEV2. Need postmortem to include why timeout behavior regressed in streaming path and why configstore DB paging spiked.
next-oncall-ryan: Handoff: monitoring alert threshold lowered for configstore pg latency. I'll follow up on DB index and query plans tomorrow. Leaving notes in PagerDuty.
oncall-alex: Thanks all. If it reappears ping channel with :rotating_light: and we re-open. Closing triage, moving to post-incident track.
incident-bot: Incident resolved: auto-close pending 30m without regression.
